## Context / Problem
A rebar client installing from source reported this minor issue alongside the archived-child claim bug (b7a2-4453-3bbd-4a54). Their pipx invocation reported that pipx needs uv>=0.9.17 while the selected host uv was 0.7.18. The failure reads like a rebar packaging problem even though the reported workaround proves it is a host pipx/uv toolchain mismatch.

## Approach
Add a troubleshooting callout in README.md section `### From source`, immediately after its source-install commands. Introduce the affected local-path pipx form, phrase the condition around seeing the observed error rather than asserting that every older uv release breaks every pipx install, and show `pipx install --backend pip "<path>[agents]"` as the workaround. State that the mismatch is not a rebar packaging defect. Local evidence recorded on the ticket confirms pipx 1.16.5 exposes `--backend {pip,uv}`; no package metadata or runtime behavior changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The README.md `### From source` section describes the observed `uv>=0.9.17` error; verified with `grep -Fq "uv>=0.9.17" README.md`.
- [ ] The same callout shows `pipx install --backend pip "<path>[agents]"`; verified with `grep -Fq -- "--backend pip" README.md`.
- [ ] The callout explicitly identifies the condition as a host pipx/uv toolchain mismatch, not a rebar packaging defect; verified by reading the rendered paragraph in its source-install context.
- [ ] Repository lint remains green; verified with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`.
